Sara Farnya <sales@avicennaresearch.com>:
Hi Janet, I'm glad to hear that you found the information helpful! Regarding your question, we are currently in the process of implementing a Pricing model that will allow a research manager to monitor a license shared among multiple researchers and studies. The system will provide real-time reports on each study's usage of the license, and we plan to release it by the end of the year. In the meantime, I'd like to suggest an alternative: As we discussed, we offer researchers a dedicated dashboard when they create a researcher account. In their dashboard, they can monitor the list of their projects from the "My Studies" page. This can include both their own projects and projects from colleagues that they have been added to as researchers. In your case, you can create a researcher account for your entire department if necessary. This way, the account admin can create the studies and then add other researchers to them as needed. Each researcher should have their own account to be added to the studies by the admin. Then, researchers can continue working on the studies, and the admin can monitor the researchers across all the projects. Please note that the admin will have access to all the project data in this case and can manage the permissions. For more information, please visit here. By the way, we don't have any limitations on the number of researchers collaborating on a study. However, researchers can be removed from the projects when needed. I assume by "deleting," you meant stopping the participants from using your quota by uninstalling the app. As mentioned in the meeting, you can simply put an end date for your studies so that they won't use your quota after that time. Please let me know if I misunderstood anything. If you have further questions, please don't hesitate to contact me. Best, Sara P.S. Sara Farnya <sales@avicennaresearch.com>:
Hi John, I hope you’re having a great weekend. My apologies for not getting back to you sooner. Thank you for reaching out with your questions. I'll address each one below: once we provide the access to the application for users how can we control their access to other studies? I believe you're asking about controlling access to the researcher dashboard and available studies for different researchers. As mentioned, you could consider setting up a single researcher account for your entire department and creating studies using it. This account will serve as the study owner for all the studies, allowing the account admin to control user access. Only the admin can invite researchers to studies and adjust their permissions as needed. Researchers will not have access to studies unless they are specifically invited. And how do we prevent them from creating additional studies?Is there a limit on the number of admin accounts? Ideally, we would like to have at least three admin accounts; One for Janet (manages IRB) and two for our IT staff to administer the users. If the proposed plan works for your team, the admin could be our main point of contact for the license, responsible for initially creating studies and granting access to other researchers. You can share the admin account's credentials with the individuals you mentioned, or with additional users if necessary. There’s no need to create multiple admin accounts, as this simplifies tracking user access. Alternatively, you could decide not to use an admin account at all. Researchers could create their studies independently and then share the study IDs with you as our main point of contact to add their studies to the license. You may also request that they invite you as a researcher to their studies, allowing you to monitor them. In this scenario, they will be the study owners, but you will still need to contact us for any upgrades. In either case, we will designate any team member you choose as the main point of contact for your license. These people will be the only ones authorized to contact us to add studies to your license. If you wish to authorize anyone besides Janet and yourself, please share their contact information with me. If you need more detailed guidance on setting this up, feel free to let me know!
